text.p: Textiles firm Gamma Holding NV said on Thursday it would halt the activities of its subsidiary Planox BV at short notice.
"The reason for this decision is the loss-making situation Planox has faced for several years," Gamma said in a statement. It added that the unit had no prospects of a profitable business in future.

Planox manufactures wall coverings and industrial coated products. In its 1995 annual report Gamma had already said the unit had been facing a difficult market situation for years and that an expected recovery had not materialised.
Planox has its production plant in the southern Dutch town of Helmond where it has 65 employees. Another nine people work in sales outlets in Brussels and London.
The unit posted 1996 turnover of 17 million guilders.
Gamma said the decision to halt Planox fitted its strategy of selling or ending activities which in the longer run are unable to contribute to the company's profits.
